blocks.text: Ezekiel 38 introduces Gog of Magog as the leader of a large coalition that attacks a restored and secure Israel, only to be defeated by divine action. The chapter therefore presents the invasion and its outcome as one unified vision. A textual question remains: Papyrus 967 places the material usually numbered Ezekiel 38–39 before chapter 37, an ancient arrangement different from the familiar Masoretic sequence.

sections.title: A question about the chapter’s setting
